GENERAL SUMMARY

Under the direction of the Shift Supervisor, and in coordination with the O&M services contract, performs the control room operation of main units and other plant equipment, and minor maintenance duties as required.

PRIMARY FUNCTIONS

  • Operates plant equipment and switchgear, which have their controls in the control room. Operates plant power units including starting up, paralleling and shutting down the main unit.
  • Places into service and removes from service various plant equipment and auxiliaries.
  • Well-versed in actions required to place plant equipment in a safe condition during emergency situations.
  • Performs, or assists in routine maintenance of equipment under his/her control; and performs in a maintenance mode when working his/her relief week (and not relieving other operators), for all overhauls, and other major maintenance-related downtimes.
  • Maintains station by way of consistent housekeeping and safety checks for potential safety hazards.
  • Assists, as required, in the training and orientation of new Control Room Operators, O&M Technicians, and Assistant Plant Operators.
  • Writes switching orders and performs necessary switching.
  • Must be available for overtime, rotating shifts, and emergency callouts.
  • Must be willing to work on a temporary basis as O&M Technician and/or Shift Supervisor.
  • Other tasks as assigned.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Physical requirements include sitting, standing and walking. Occasional periods of lifting and climbing.

All employees will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program. This program includes a post-offer physical examination and drug screening and post employment random drug screening. There are extensive smoking restrictions in and around the facility.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum four (4) years experience in power plant operator functions, to include demonstrated experience in operating a power plant control room and all related auxiliary functions. High school diploma, or equivalent, required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of all facets of the principles of power production, control room operation, including knowledge of maintenance functions as relates to the control room, operating procedures, system operating orders, and clearance procedures.
  • Demonstrated ability to clear equipment, write switching orders, and perform necessary switching.
  • Good communication skills.

We are currently looking for a Cost Management Lead to join our team

Purpose of the Role

The Cost Management Lead is the developer and owner of the cost control function at Keel Infrastructure. This role stands up centralized cost management as a service to the business — building the estimating methodology, the standards, the cost data, and the tooling from the ground up, and then running that service across every data center project in the portfolio. This is a hands-on delivery role for someone who has personally controlled cost on projects through to close-out and wants to build the function, not inherit it.

Key Responsibilities

Function Development & Centralized Cost Control

  • Establish and own the centralized cost control function for Keel Infrastructure, defining its scope, service model, and interface with development, project management, scheduling, procurement, and finance.
  • Serve as the single owner of the cost plan of record for every project in the portfolio, maintaining budgets centrally rather than leaving them distributed across contractors and project teams.
  • Build the cost management toolset and environment — cost breakdown structures, code of accounts, chart of accounts alignment, and system configuration — so cost rolls up cleanly from commitment to portfolio level.

Estimating & Concept Stage Cost Planning

  • Develop concept, order-of-magnitude, and feasibility estimates for prospective sites, translating limited early information into credible, benchmark-backed cost plans with clearly stated basis of estimate and confidence ranges.
  • Cost model site-specific drivers at concept stage — utility interconnection, substation and power infrastructure, site works, permitting, and constructability constraints.
  • Support site selection, capital planning, and investment approval with comparative cost scenarios, $/MW analysis, and sensitivity testing.

Budget Ownership & Delivery Stage Cost Management

  • Own the project budget and cost report through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and final account, maintaining continuity from the concept-stage baseline.
  • Manage commitments, accruals, cash flow forecasts, and cost-to-complete across all packages, contractors, vendors, and consultants.
  • Review and challenge contractor cost reports, pay applications, schedules of values, and invoices; verify progress claims against installed work and earned value.
  • Manage contingency and allowance drawdown with clear governance over what is released, when, and against what justification.

Process, Procedure & Standards Development

  • Author and roll out the cost management processes, procedures, and templates used across the portfolio — estimate development and approval, budget baselining, monthly cost reporting, accrual, forecasting, and change control.
  • Define cost reporting and commercial requirements for contractor and consultant agreements, then review submissions against those requirements and reject non-conforming reports.

Cost Database Development & Benchmarking

  • Build and own the historical cost database, capturing actual unit rates, package costs, and final account outcomes from every completed and in-flight project.
  • Develop the benchmark set that underpins concept-stage estimating: $/MW, $/sqft, package-level unit rates, and realistic ranges rather than single-point assumptions.
  • Variance analysis between benchmark, estimate, tender, and final outcome, and feed those findings back into estimating assumptions and procedures.

Change Management & Commercial Control

  • Lead the change control process end to end — identification, pricing, assessment, negotiation, approval, and incorporation into the cost plan of record.
  • Independently price and challenge contractor change order submissions; negotiate commercial settlements and defend the owner's position on entitlement.

Forecasting, Reporting & Analytics

  • Produce portfolio-level cost dashboards, variance analysis, and narrative reporting for project leadership and senior executives.
  • Own forecast accuracy: maintain cost-to-complete and estimate-at-completion positions that hold up, with variance explained and quantified rather than discovered late.
  • Integrate cost with schedule to produce earned value, cash flow curves, and time-phased spend forecasts alongside the Program Scheduler.
  • Partner with Finance on capitalization, funding drawdown, capital plan alignment, and month-end close.

Requirements

Experience & Background

  • 10+ years of cost management, quantity surveying, or project controls experience on large capital construction programs, with demonstrable hands-on delivery — not reporting-only experience.
  • Direct experience building or substantially rebuilding a cost control function, including the processes, standards, tooling, and data behind it.
  • Proven experience developing concept and preconstruction estimates that informed real capital and site selection decisions.
  • Experience carrying budgets through the full delivery lifecycle to final account and close-out.
  • Demonstrated ownership of change management and commercial negotiation on complex, multi-package builds.
  • Experience on programs of $200M+ in total installed cost; data center, mission-critical, hyperscale, HPC, heavy industrial, or utility-scale experience strongly preferred, owner or developer side preferred.

Technical Knowledge

  • Expert knowledge of earned value management, cash flow forecasting, and cost-to-complete methodologies.
  • Deep familiarity with contract structures (GMP, lump sum, design-build, CMAR) and their payment, change, and claims provisions.
  • Data structuring and analytics capability — Power BI, SQL, or equivalent — sufficient to build and query a benchmarking database.
  • Proficiency with cost management and finance systems.
  • Understanding of data center design and construction: electrical distribution, power systems, mechanical cooling, structural and civil packages, and their cost drivers.
  • Sound financial acumen and the ability to interface credibly with senior finance and executive teams.

Delivery & Competencies

  • Builder's mindset — comfortable operating with no existing framework and creating the standard rather than applying someone else's.
  • Strong commercial judgment and negotiation skills; willing to hold a firm position with contractors and defend it with data.
  • Drives accountability across internal and external teams without formal authority.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to make a complex cost position understandable to non-commercial audiences.

Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, Finance, or a related field.
  • Professional certifications or memberships related to role are preferred.

Key Success Metrics

Performance in this role will be evaluated against the following outcomes:

  • Function established — A centralized cost control function operating as a recognised service to the business, with documented processes, standards, and tooling in place and in use.
  • Estimate credibility — Concept and preconstruction estimates that hold up against tender returns and final outcomes, with basis of estimate traceable and variance explained.
  • Budget performance — Projects delivered within approved budget and variance thresholds, with disciplined contingency and allowance management.
  • Forecast accuracy — Cost-to-complete and estimate-at-completion positions that hold up over time, with deviation surfaced early rather than at close-out.
  • Change control integrity — All changes are identified, independently priced, and settled on defensible commercial terms with full traceability.
  • Stakeholder confidence — Clear, consistent reporting and strong working relationships with development, construction, procurement, finance, and external partners.

Work Arrangement

  • Location: New York Office
  • Schedule: On-site a minimum of three (3) days per week.
  • Travel: Periodic travel to project sites, vendor facilities, and partner locations as required.

The base salary range is $165,000-$205,000. Our total compensation package combines this base salary with a bonus target and participates in our yearly equity grant. We offer a fantastic benefits package and many perks. There's a top-down emphasis on amazing work culture at our organization.

We are currently looking for a Director, Data Center Electrical Engineering to join our team!

Purpose of the Role

The Director of Data Center Electrical Engineering is a senior leadership role responsible for defining, owning, and continuously advancing the company's electrical engineering standards across all data center development projects. This individual serves as the internal authority on power distribution architecture, backup power systems, medium-voltage infrastructure, controls integration, and electrical system reliability — ensuring that every facility we develop is engineered to deliver the power capacity, redundancy, and efficiency our customers and business require.

This role partners closely with mechanical engineering, commissioning, construction management, procurement, and utility relations teams to drive coordinated electrical design decisions from site selection and utility engagement through design, construction, and energization. The Director of Electrical Engineering sets the frameworks, specifications, and design standards that govern how our portfolio is powered — and ensures those standards are consistently applied and continuously improved as the company scales and as customer requirements evolve toward higher-density, AI-driven workloads.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Leadership & Standards

  • Develop and own the company's electrical engineering design standards, basis-of-design documentation, and technical specifications governing all electrical systems across new data center development.
  • Establish and enforce electrical design criteria for critical power path systems: utility service entrance, medium-voltage switchgear, unit substation transformers, low-voltage switchgear and switchboards, UPS systems, static transfer switches (STS), PDUs, and IT busway/whip distribution.
  • Define standards for backup power infrastructure including diesel generator plants, automatic transfer switches (ATS), and battery energy storage systems (BESS).
  • Drive continuous improvement of power usage effectiveness (PUE) through efficient electrical system design, transformer loss optimization, and power factor management.
  • Lead evaluation, selection, and standardization of electrical equipment and systems across the portfolio to maximize reliability, reduce spare parts complexity, and improve procurement leverage.

Project Execution

  • Provide electrical engineering leadership and technical review across all project phases, from site feasibility and schematic design through design development, construction documents, and commissioning.
  • Review and approve electrical design packages from external engineers of record (EORs), ensuring compliance with company standards, NEC, NFPA 70/75/76, and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Oversee the development of single-line diagrams, system architectures, and load schedules as living design documents throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Lead electrical value engineering efforts, balancing first cost, lifecycle cost, equipment lead times, reliability, and schedule across each project.
  • Support RFP development, bid evaluation, and contractor/vendor selection for electrical scopes of work; review electrical subcontractor qualifications and proposed means and methods.
  • Oversee electrical construction administration including submittal review, RFI responses, field design changes, and coordination with the commissioning team during startup and energization.

Team & Stakeholder Management

  • Build, mentor, and lead an internal electrical engineering team as the company's development pipeline grows.
  • Manage relationships with external electrical engineers of record, specialty consultants (protection and relay, arc flash, power quality), equipment manufacturers, and utility contacts.
  • Collaborate with mechanical engineering to coordinate power requirements for cooling infrastructure, including chilled water plant electrical loads, VFD integration, and BMS/EPMS power interfaces.
  • Partner with commissioning to ensure electrical systems are designed for testability, including provisions for temporary load banks, metering points, relay test switches, and isolation capability for IST.
  • Present electrical design strategies, system architecture decisions, and capital investment recommendations to executive leadership and, where applicable, to customers and investors.

Innovation & Technology Roadmap

  • Evaluate and develop the company's strategy for high-density power distribution to support AI/HPC workloads — including 415V busway, direct 480V rack-level distribution, high-ampacity overhead busway systems, and 800VDC integration.
  • Develop roadmap for integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) to support grid resiliency, demand response, and sustainability goals.
  • Monitor and respond to evolving NEC, NFPA, IEEE, and utility interconnection requirements across key development markets; update company standards accordingly.
  • Participate in relevant industry organizations (7x24 Exchange, NFPA, IEEE, Uptime Institute) and contribute to thought leadership.

Requirements

Experience & Background

  • 12+ years of progressive electrical engineering experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading electrical design on hyperscale, colocation, or enterprise data center projects.
  • Experience as a technical owner or discipline lead, not just a contributor, on large capital projects.
  • Prior experience managing or mentoring engineering staff and external consultants.

Technical Knowledge

  • Deep knowledge of data center electrical distribution architectures.
  • Proficiency in medium-voltage system design.
  • Strong knowledge of UPS systems, battery systems, and static and mechanical transfer switch technologies.
  • Experience with backup power systems including diesel generator sizing, fuel systems, and generator controls integration.
  • Experience with electrical system modeling, including arc flash hazard analysis (NFPA 70E), short circuit studies, load flow analysis, and power quality assessments.
  • Familiarity with SCADA, EPMS, and BMS integration requirements for electrical infrastructure monitoring and control.

Leadership & Competencies

  • Ability to translate complex electrical engineering concepts for non-technical audiences including executives and investors.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; experience authoring design standards and technical specifications.
  • Collaborative mindset with experience working cross-functionally in fast-paced development environments.

Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor’s in Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license strongly preferred.
  • Professional certifications (CDCDP, PMP, ATD, LEED AP, DCEP, or similar) are a significant asset.

Key Success Metrics

Performance in this role will be evaluated against the following outcomes:

  • Standards Development — Publish company-wide electrical design standards.
  • PUE Performance — Achieve or exceed target annualized PUE for new facilities.
  • Design Schedule Adherence — Electrical design packages issued on schedule, measured against approved project milestones.
  • Quality outcomes — Facility delivered to Keel’s design specifications and critical infrastructure standards, with complete documentation and as-builts at handover.
  • Commissioning readiness — Successful L0–L5 commissioning execution and timely system handover to operations teams.
  • Stakeholder confidence — Clear, consistent, and accurate reporting to the VP of Engineering and senior leadership; strong working relationships with the owner’s rep, GC, engineering partners, and municipal stakeholders.
  • Risk management — Proactive identification and mitigation of project risks ahead of critical path impact.

Work Arrangement

  • Location: Remote
  • Schedule: On-site (NYC HQ) a minimum of one week per month.
  • Travel: Occasional travel to other Keel sites or vendor/partner locations as required.

We are currently looking for a Schedule Management Lead to join our team

Purpose of the Role

The Schedule Management Lead is the developer and owner of the scheduling function at Keel Infrastructure. The role stands up centralized schedule management as a service to the business — building the methodology, standards, data, and tooling from the ground up, then running that service across the portfolio. This is a hands-on delivery role for someone who has personally driven projects to completion and wants to build the function, not inherit it.

Key Responsibilities

Function Development & Centralized Schedule Management

  • Establish and own the centralized scheduling function for Keel Infrastructure, defining its scope, service model, and interface with development, project management, project controls, procurement, and finance.
  • Set up and manage the plan of record for every project in the portfolio, maintaining schedules centrally rather than leaving them distributed across contractors and project teams.
  • Build the scheduling toolset and environment — enterprise structure, EPS/WBS hierarchy, coding dictionaries, calendars, layouts, and security — so schedules roll up cleanly from activity to portfolio level.
  • Own execution planning alongside scheduling — define the work breakdown and packaging strategy, delivery sequencing logic, and phasing approach for each project before logic is built, so the schedule reflects a deliberate plan rather than a transcription of contractor intent.
  • Maintain the multi-year portfolio delivery plan, sequencing projects against capital availability, resource capacity, and utility timing so development and finance plan against a single roadmap.

Preconstruction & Concept Stage Scheduling

  • Develop concept and feasibility-stage schedules for prospective sites, translating limited early information into credible, benchmark-backed duration and milestone assumptions.
  • Model entitlement, permitting, utility interconnection, and power energization paths at concept stage, and quantify their impact on ready-for-service dates.
  • Support site selection, capital planning, and investment approval with schedule scenarios, comparative site timelines, and sensitivity analysis.

Delivery Stage Schedule Management

  • Own the integrated master schedule through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational turnover, maintaining continuity from the concept-stage baseline.
  • Integrate contractor, vendor, A&E, utility, and long-lead equipment schedules into a single program plan, resolving interface conflicts across packages.
  • Align the schedule to the commissioning plan and L0–L5 requirements to protect handover dates.

Process, Procedure & Standards Development

  • Author and roll out the scheduling processes, procedures, and templates used across the portfolio — baseline approval, update cycles, progress measurement, change control, and quality gates.
  • Define schedule specification requirements for contractor and consultant agreements, then review submissions against those requirements and reject non-conforming schedules.
  • Apply structured schedule quality checks (DCMA 14-point or equivalent) as a gate on every baseline and update.

Database Development & Benchmarking

  • Build and own the historical schedule database and WBS structure, capturing actual durations, sequences, productivity rates, and milestone performance from every completed and in-flight project.
  • Develop the benchmark set that underpins concept-stage planning: standard durations by scope and package, typical critical path shapes, and realistic ranges rather than single-point assumptions.
  • Maintain reference and template schedules for standard data center product types so new projects start from proven logic instead of a blank page.

Progress Tracking & Performance Measurement

  • Own progress measurement across the portfolio: define rules of credit, physical percent complete methodologies, and earned progress curves by package and discipline.
  • Produce and interpret performance metrics — SPI, float consumption, critical path movement, milestone slippage, and installation rates — and convert them into recovery recommendations.
  • Validate contractor-reported progress against field verification, installed quantities, and commissioning readiness rather than accepting reported percentages at face value.

Risk, Change & Reporting

  • Maintain schedule risk registers and run quantitative schedule risk analysis to size contingency and test milestone confidence levels.
  • Assess time impact of change orders, RFIs, design revisions, weather, and utility delays; prepare and review time impact analyses and support delay claim evaluation.
  • Enforce schedule change governance so every revision to the plan of record is documented, justified, and traceable.
  • Produce portfolio-level schedule dashboards and narrative reporting for project leadership and senior executives.

Requirements

Experience & Background

  • 10+ years of scheduling and project controls experience on large capital construction programs, with demonstrable hands-on project delivery — not reporting-only experience.
  • Direct experience building or substantially rebuilding a scheduling function, including the processes, standards, tooling, and data behind it.
  • Proven experience developing concept and preconstruction-stage schedules that inform real capital and site selection decisions.
  • Experience managing schedules through the full delivery lifecycle to commissioning and turnover, with personal accountability for milestone delivery.
  • Track record building or using historical schedule databases and benchmark data to set and defend duration assumptions.
  • Data center, mission-critical, hyperscale, HPC, heavy industrial, or utility-scale project experience strongly preferred; owner, developer, or program management side preferred.

Technical Knowledge

  • Expert-level Primavera P6, including enterprise/EPS configuration, multi-project structures, global change, and baseline management; Microsoft Project and Smartsheet preferred.
  • Deep command of CPM scheduling theory: logic, float, calendars, constraints, critical and near-critical path analysis, and schedule compression techniques.
  • Working knowledge of earned value management, time impact analysis, and quantitative schedule risk analysis (Monte Carlo).
  • Data structuring and analytics capability — Power BI, SQL, or equivalent — sufficient to build and query a benchmarking database.
  • Understanding data center design and construction: electrical distribution, power systems, mechanical cooling, structural and civil packages, and utility interconnection sequencing.

Delivery & Competencies

  • Builder's mindset — comfortable operating with no existing framework and creating the standard rather than applying someone else's.
  • Drives accountability across internal and external teams without formal authority.
  • Highly analytical, with the judgment to distinguish reporting noise from real schedule risk.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to make a complex schedule understandable to non-schedulers.

Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related field.
  • Professional certifications related to role are preferred.

Key Success Metrics

  • Function established — A centralized scheduling function operating as a recognised service to the business, with documented processes, standards, and tooling in place and in use.
  • Concept-stage credibility — Preconstruction and concept schedules that hold up as projects mature, with early assumptions traceable and variance explained.
  • Continuity of the plan of record — A single owned schedule carried from concept through turnover without re-baselining to mask slippage.
  • Milestone adherence — On-time delivery of key milestones from entitlement and energization through commissioning and turnover.

Work Arrangement

  • Location: New York Office
  • Schedule: On-site a minimum of three (3) days per week.
  • Travel: Periodic travel to Keel Infrastructure project sites, vendor facilities, and partner locations as required.

GENERAL SUMMARY

The Shift Supervisor is responsible during his/her shift for all personnel and equipment involved in the production of steam and electricity at the plant. He or she plans, coordinates, supervises, monitors, and controls all on-shift operations, material handling, and related maintenance and engineering activities working with the various departments. As the senior individual on duty around the clock, he or she has the responsibility and authority to take whatever actions may be necessary to protect people and equipment, such as reducing load, taking boilers out-of-service, or taking the turbine generator off-line.

PRIMARY FUNCTIONS

  • Ensure safe operation of the power plant and safety all personnel on site.
  • Ensure that the plant is operated in compliance with all Environmental Permits, Regulations, Laws and Company Policies.
  • Provides direct supervision to plant operations personnel.
  • Assists the Ops Manager and O&M Coordinator in all facets of department administration and power plant management.
  • Conducts routine tours of the plant to inspect equipment; provide direction, supervision and feedback to employees; and ensures that all safety rules and plant procedures are followed.
  • Inspects all Mine Safety and Health Administration Regulated, (MSHA), areas of the power plant at least once per shift.
  • Reviews plant operating logs such as Shift Supervisor log, O&M Tech log, Loader Log and Chemistry log at least once per shift and ensures actions are taken to correct any noted deficiencies.
  • Maintains complete and accurate reports of downtime, outages, repair requirements, and production and performance indices.
  • Plans, directs, and performs functional testing of plant systems and components. Interprets data based on established standards and/or sound power plant practices.
  • Investigates plant problems, incidents, accidents, and unusual events, and provides analyses, recommendations, reports, and appropriate follow-up plans.
  • Checks daily consumption rates of chemicals, gases, fuels, water, and other consumables; monitors inventories and initiates action to replenish same.
  • Verifies all in-plant switching and tagging of equipment in accordance with approved procedures and prudent operations and maintenance practices.
  • Plans, directs and performs/manages housekeeping duties. Ensures housekeeping standards are maintained and initiates corrective action, as required.
  • Writes, reviews, and revises operating and related procedures. Ensures procedural compliance in the conduct of plant operations, maintenance, and personnel administration.
  • Plans, directs, and supervises routine preventive and predictive maintenance on all systems and equipment; supports corrective maintenance efforts on selected equipment.

Pour soutenir ses opérations croissantes, Keel Infrastructure est à la recherche de techniciens-nes IOC pour effectuer entre autres des interventions sur les systèmes d’alimentation, de refroidissement, de calcul, de réseau et de sécurité incendie.

Plus précisément, tu auras à:

  • Assurer la surveillance en temps réels des tableaux de bord sur l’ensemble des sites Keel, incluant les systèmes d’alimentation (UPS, PDU, appareillage de connexion, générateurs), de refroidissement (CRAC/CRAH), les capteurs environnementaux, le réseau et sécurité incendie (VESDA, état de la suppression).
  • Répondre et traiter les alertes automatisées dans les délais prescrits par les ententes de niveau de service (SLA), effectuer le triage selon les runbooks, analyser les tendances dans Grafana, SCADA, BMS et ION, et déterminer les actions appropriées : intervention directe, escalade ou déploiement sur site.
  • Prendre en charge les incidents; de la détection à la résolution: analyser la cause profonde, classifier la gravité (P1–P4), coordonner avec les équipes sur site et les fournisseurs, et s’assurer qu’aucun incident ne quitte le quart sans propriétaire désigné et statut clair.
  • Rédiger des rapports de quart précis et complets, afin de garantir à l'équipe entrante une vue d'ensemble claire des incidents en cours, des escalades en attente et des risques identifiés sur site.
  • Assurer le contrôle des accès aux sites, gérer l'armement et le désarmement des systèmes de sécurité selon les horaires établis, et signaler toute activité non autorisée ou anormale.
  • Identifier les tendances récurrentes et contribuer à l'amélioration continue des runbooks et des procédures opérationnelles.

Pour te qualifier pour le poste, il faut:

  • Expérience en infrastructure électrique ou domaine connexe, que ce soit en surveillance, en dépannage ou sur le terrain.
  • Aisance avec la lecture de tableaux de bord et le triage d’alertes, avec une expérience sur Grafana, Zabbix ou équivalent.
  • Rigueur dans la gestion des systèmes de billetterie: documentation exhaustive et suivi des dossiers jusqu'à leur fermeture (Jira, ServiceNow, ou équivalent).
  • Aptitude à rédiger des communications écrites claires et structurées sous pression, notamment les notes de quart et les rapports de passation.
  • Connaissances de base en réseau : commutation, routage et dépannage de connectivité.

Vous vous démarquez si vous avez:

  • Une expérience dans un NOC, IOC, centre de données, environnement de colocation ou secteur lié à l’énergie.
  • Une exposition au minage de Bitcoin, au calcul haute densité ou aux systèmes OT industriels (SCADA, BMS, ION).
  • Une familiarité avec les systèmes de suppression d’incendie (VESDA, FM200) ou des solutions de refroidissement de précision.
  • Une certification en cours ou obtenue; CompTIA A+, Network+, DCDC ou équivalent.

Autres informations:

  • Voyage requis: possibilités de déplacement entre les sites et installations au Québec.
  • Horaire de travail: flexible, semaine ou fin de la semaine
  • Type de poste: temps plein, temps partiel.
